newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa trade data seen promising despite deficit.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa trade data seen promising despite deficit.

text.p: South African February trade figures showed encouraging signs of continuing growth in manufacturing exports, despite the overall trade balance slide into deficit in the month, economists said on Thursday.
The data showed the country's trade balance swung from a 517 million rand surplus in January to a 452 million rand shortfall in February.
This was well off a consensus forecast for a 1.04 billion rand surplus for the month and a billion rand below even the most pessimistic forecast of a 500 million rand surplus.
"But there is some good news and that is that on the export side all the top five categories are manufacturing items," E.W. Balderson economist Mike Schussler said.

He said the transport exports category had shown a 112.4 percent increase, miscellaneous manufacturing a 73.4 percent rise, food and beverages 42 percent growth and the shoes and textiles categories 34.4 percent and 28.7 percent increases respectively.
Economists are pinning hopes of a gross domestic product growth rate of around 2.5 percent this year on an export-led recovery in the manufacturing sector.
